source.title: Deep Dreams Are Made of This: Visualizing Monosemantic Features in Diffusion Models

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables and figure contents are flattened or omitted in the text extraction, but the reported qualitative results and relevant descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper qualitatively evaluates whether SAE dictionary features in a diffusion model yield coherent, stable interpretations, using optimized visualizations and dataset examples rather than testing superposition geometry or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper compares SAE features with raw layer channels and reports visualization outcomes relevant to the interpretability and stability portion of V5. It does not test feature completeness or canonicality. Hyperparameter values used to select settings, cited results, and regularizer sweeps unrelated to feature-unit interpretability are not separate rows. The regularization-dependent change for SAE feature 14 is included because the paper explicitly reports a changed feature interpretation.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a feature-visualization method (LVO) for Stable Diffusion 1.5. It uses pre-trained SAeUron SAEs as a tool and reports qualitative visualization quality. The SAE-versus-raw-channel comparison is a hand-picked, qualitative showcase of the method in a diffusion U-Net, not an LLM, so it does not measure V4. It does not test V5's completeness, canonicality, or stability across SAE training. Its 'consistency across seeds' refers to seeds of the visualization prior, not to SAE features. The finding goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LVO extends feature visualization to latent diffusion models. They find SAE features yield clearer, more consistent visualizations than raw channels, which they also read as evidence that the SAE disentangles the layer into meaningful features. They find pixel-space regularizers transfer but need different settings for the raw-layer and SAE variants, and that LVO complements dataset examples and steering. They caveat that features may be multifaceted and that results are bounded by SAE quality.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE-based feature visualization and a raw-channel comparison in a latent diffusion model; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method or measure overlapping feature geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretations vary by activity peak, random seed, and regularization configuration. The paper reports feature 10331 producing plain images at t = 121, and feature 14 changing from a muddy texture to a cable-like structure under stronger transformation robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: In the up1.1 layer of SD 1.5 (Style50), raw channels yielded mixed or seed-dependent visualizations with varied dataset examples. Selected SAE features yielded coherent, consistent visualizations matching more uniform dataset examples. The evidence is qualitative and drawn from hand-picked case studies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion-model U-Nets, raw channels are polysemantic while SAE dictionary features are more monosemantic (a diffusion analogue of V4).

record.problems: Evaluation is qualitative, with no accepted interpretability metric or reported statistical uncertainty. Empirical scope is one model, one layer, and the first 30 raw channels and SAE features; detailed case studies cover selected features. The authors note possible multifaceted features and dependence on SAE disentanglement quality.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted. Calibration sweeps are not separately recorded except for the feature 14 interpretation change, because their reported outcomes primarily select optimization settings rather than test the claim about feature units.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy models or geometry.
All parts: no LLMs. The diffusion-model evidence that raw channels are polysemantic while SAE features look monosemantic is recorded under fits_no_version.
Completeness, stability across SAE training runs or sizes, and canonicality are all untested. Only visualizations of selected features were inspected qualitatively.

record.verdict_notes: Evaluation is qualitative, on one model and one layer, with case-study features selected by the authors. The SAEs come from SAeUron and were not trained here. The record's V5 'supports' label conflates the visualization's seed consistency with the stability of SAE features as units.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether they are evidence of superposition.
LLMs, feature spread across neurons, and sparse features recovered by dictionaries or SAEs in LLMs.

The study examines qualitative interpretability and consistency across selected peaks and seeds, but does not establish SAE features as complete or canonical units, test completeness of the dictionary, or evaluate stability beyond one model, one layer, and selected features.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively assessed SAE feature 9984 visualizations against dataset examples across activity peaks.
rows.measure: Qualitative interpretability and consistency of optimized visualization with dataset examples
rows.value: Visualization showed delicate colorful strokes oriented top-left to bottom-right; dataset examples shared the diagonal composition. Strongest activation was 10.6 at t = 301.
rows.note: The paper reports that the visualization was consistent across activity peaks and random seeds; it says the dataset images shared the diagonal arrangement despite varying in content.
rows.check: Measures how interpretable an optimized visualization is, using prior seeds, not SAE feature stability or canonicality. The value 10.6 is the visualization's activation, compared with a normal maximum of 3-4.

rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively assessed SAE feature 9984 visualization at another activity peak against dataset examples.
rows.measure: Qualitative interpretability and consistency of optimized visualization with dataset examples
rows.value: Visualization showed the diagonal-composition pattern; activation at the other time steps was reported in the 7–8 range.
rows.note: The authors describe the feature as appearing monosemantic across all activity peaks.
rows.check: Same issue as r1. The 7-8 activation is reached by the optimized visualization. It is not a result on V5.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature 14 visualizations under different transformation-robustness regularization levels with dataset examples.
rows.measure: Qualitative feature interpretation and correspondence with dataset examples
rows.baseline: Weak regularization produced a muddy crowd-like texture.
rows.value: Stronger transformation robustness produced a cable-like structure also present in dataset examples.
rows.locator: Section 4; Sections F and G.7; Figure 14
rows.note: The interpretation changed with regularization; the authors suggest regularization may help escape an uninterpretable local maximum and reveal a more meaningful facet.
rows.check: This is a calibration-sweep observation: the regularizer setting changes the visualization. It reflects sensitivity of the visualization method, not of the SAE feature. The same change also occurred under the range and moment penalties (G.9, G.10).

rows.note: This raw-channel result is a comparator about polysemantic visualizations, not a direct test of whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units.

reader_labels.condition: SAE feature 9984 at t = 301, 541, and 661; SAE feature 10331 at t = 381 and 621
reader_labels.reason: The visualizations were reported as coherent and consistent with dataset examples across the stated peaks, and the authors describe these features as more monosemantic than the raw-layer baseline (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SAE feature 10331 at t = 121 and SAE feature 14 under varying transformation robustness
reader_labels.reason: One peak for feature 10331 produced plain images rather than the reported human figure, and feature 14's interpretation changed with regularization; the results therefore do not establish universally stable, canonical feature interpretations (r6–r7).
